synopsis: NVIDIA RTX is a consumer and workstation graphics-card line with dedicated ray-tracing cores; vendor RTX sensor-simulation platforms use GPU ray tracing with material interaction [f16194, f4928]. One vendor claims its current RTX lidar implementation accounts for transparent and reflective surfaces, but no neutral benchmark applicable to the collision-mitigation validation program was found [f4510, f4929]. The tools chapter reports vendor claims that open-source platforms combining Unreal Engine 5 rendering and RTX sensors exist and are free for internal use [f9336, f9337]. The lowest-cost example chain uses on-premises RTX GPUs or spot cloud computing, with the glossary additionally describing scenario scripts or Scenic and J1939 emulation to ISO/TS 21815-2 [f9268, f16159]. For this lowest-cost open-source-core chain, the manufacturer must characterize RTX sensor performance issues, leaving validation responsibility with the manufacturer despite the available platforms and vendor capabilities claimed [f9282, f4929, f4510].

relations.note: Both specify on-premises RTX hardware or spot cloud for the lowest-cost chain.
Dedicated ray-tracing cores underpin the GPU ray tracing used by vendor sensor platforms.
The lidar claim specifies transparent and reflective surfaces within material interaction.
Absent applicable neutral benchmarks reinforce the need for manufacturer performance characterization.
Using the lowest-cost RTX chain requires manufacturer characterization of sensor performance issues.
Adds free internal-use terms to the reported availability of these platforms.
